arguments.new_string:
def test_release_1_0_empty_statement(self):
        got = self.run_cli({"command": "statement", "release": "1.0", "lines": []})
        self.assertEqual(got, {"release": "1.0", "lines": [], "credit_cents": 0, "amount_due_cents": 0})

    def test_release_1_0_one_line_receipt_example(self):
        got = self.run_cli({"command": "statement", "release": "1.0",
                            "lines": [line("L-1", charge=19999)]})
        self.assertEqual(got, {"release": "1.0", "credit_cents": 1999, "amount_due_cents": 18000,
                               "lines": [response_line("L-1", 1999, 18000)]})
        self.assertEqual(set(got), {"release", "lines", "credit_cents", "amount_due_cents"})

    def test_release_1_0_priority_is_earliest_service_date_then_line_id(self):
        # Release 1.0 draws on the cap earliest service_on first, ties by line_id,
        # regardless of charge size. Output stays in input order.
        lines = [line("L-c", service_on="2026-04-10", charge=30000),
                 line("L-b", service_on="2026-04-01", charge=12000),
                 line("L-a", service_on="2026-04-01", charge=15000)]
        got = self.run_cli({"command": "statement", "release": "1.0", "lines": lines})
        self.assertEqual(got["lines"], [response_line("L-c", 0, 30000),
                                        response_line("L-b", 900, 11100),
                                        response_line("L-a", 1500, 13500)])
        self.assertEqual(got["credit_cents"], 2400)
        self.assertEqual(got["amount_due_cents"], 54600)

    def test_release_1_0_cap_is_shared_across_an_accounts_subscriptions(self):
        lines = [line("L-1", subscription="S1", charge=30000),
                 line("L-2", subscription="S2", service_on="2026-04-16", charge=30000),
                 line("L-3", account="B", subscription="S1", charge=30000)]
        got = self.run_cli({"command": "statement", "release": "1.0", "lines": lines})
        self.assertEqual(got["lines"], [response_line("L-1", 2400, 27600),
                                        response_line("L-2", 0, 30000),
                                        response_line("L-3", 2400, 27600)])
        self.assertEqual(got["credit_cents"], 4800)

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/mem10.txt <<'EOF'
Meridian Credits release "1.0" loyalty credit agreement (Finance-approved; source: issue trial-896 description). Applies to every consumer of release 1.0 (single-line quote, full-statement total, and itemized statement). Release "1.0" is the initial agreement; an omitted request release selects the current agreement (release "2.0" since issue trial-fxq), an explicit supported release selects that version, and versions introduced in an issue stay supported afterward. Public suites send explicit release values, so an earlier-release suite stays valid when the current agreement changes.

Charge line: exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id (nonempty strings; line_id unique per request), service_on (YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01..2099-12-31, never excludes a line), charge_cents (nonnegative integer US cents). Subscription identity is the pair (account_id, subscription_id); a subscription may have several lines. Each request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order = Unicode code-point order. Do not add response keys beyond those specified.

Credit rules (release 1.0): uncapped credit per line = floor(charge_cents * 10 / 100), rounded down separately per line. Cap = 2400 cents shared by all lines with the same account_id across its subscriptions; distinct accounts have independent caps. Priority within a cap group: earliest service_on first, ties by increasing line_id; charge size plays no role in priority. Each line gets its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines get only the remainder or zero. total_credit = sum of assigned credits; line amount due = charge - assigned credit; total due = total charges - total credit.

quote command: {"command":"quote","line":LINE} optionally with "release":"1.0". Response has exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; a one-line quote treats the line as the entire statement. Unsupported release -> {"error":"unsupported_release"}.

total command (issue trial-aiw): {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...]} optionally with "release":"1.0". Response has exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents for the whole charge set; the account cap is applied across all supplied lines (not a collection of independent single-line quotes). Empty statement -> {"release":"1.0","credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}. quote remains available alongside total.

statement command with explicit "release":"1.0" (issue trial-525, partner itemized receipts; a consumer of this agreement, not a new agreement): request {"command":"statement","release":"1.0","lines":[LINE,...]}. Response has exactly the existing statement shape: release, lines, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; each response line has exactly line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; lines keep the input order (priority only decides credit assignment, never output order). Uses the original 1.0 cap scope (per account_id across subscriptions) and 1.0 priority (earliest service_on, then line_id). Empty lines -> {"release":"1.0","lines":[],"credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}. One-line example, charge 19999 -> {"release":"1.0","credit_cents":1999,"amount_due_cents":18000,"lines":[{"line_id":"L-1","credit_cents":1999,"amount_due_cents":18000}]}. Statement with omitted release remains the current agreement (2.0).

Implementation: main.py RELEASES["1.0"] holds rate_percent 10, cap_cents 2400, group_key account_id, priority (service_on, line_id); assign_credits(lines, release) is the shared engine for quote(), total() and statement(). Verified 2026-09-07 by tests/test_quote.py, tests/test_total.py, tests/test_statement.py (release 1.0 cases: empty, one-line example, service-date priority, account-wide cap), public_tests/release_1_quote.json, release_1_total.json and release_1_statement.json (all passing).
EOF
bd remember "$(cat /tmp/mem10.txt)" --key 'meridian-credits/release-1.0-credit-agreement' 2>&1 | tail -3

import subprocess
s = subprocess.run(["bd", "recall", "meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agreement"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.rstrip("\n")
old = 'Implementation judgment (inference from the general "explicit supported release selects that version" rule, not a separate Finance approval): statement with explicit release "1.0" is accepted and computed under the 1.0 agreement, same as quote/total.'

Statement with omitted release stays 2.0.'
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)
s = s.replace("tests/test_smoke.py (52 tests)", "tests/test_smoke.py (56 tests)")
s = s.replace("release_2_quote_total.json, release_2_statement.json (all passing)", "release_1_statement.json, release_2_quote_total.json, release_2_statement.json (all passing)")
r = subprocess.run(["bd", "remember", s, "--key", "meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agreement"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(r.stdout[-200:], r.stderr[-200:])
back = subprocess.run(["bd", "recall", "meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agreement"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
print("has trial-525:", "trial-525" in back, "| old inference gone:", "Implementation judgment" not in back, "| 56 tests:", "56 tests" in back)
